records.name: channelscope.s2.gnomad_ryr1_missense
records.description: S2's facts, the comparator's size: RYR1's missense variants in gnomAD's dataset gnomad_r4, placed on human RyR1's residues through release exon_map_v0.5.1, with the frequencies each candidate definition of 'common' needs. It selects the single-base substitutions whose consequence, as gnomAD serves it for transcript ENST00000359596, includes missense_variant. It checks the release's files against the release's manifest, and that the release's coding sequence translates by the standard code to its protein and a stop (K0); the gnomAD answer against its retrieval record (K1); the answer's gene, RYR1 with MANE Select ENST00000359596.8 = NM_000540.3, and that the answer carries no GraphQL errors (K2); then each selected variant against the release: a coding base (K3), the reference base (K4), the c. name (K5), the residue and its amino acid (K6), the new amino acid (K7) and a missense change (K8). A planted fault for each of K1 to K8 must be caught, and the unfaulted variant they are planted in must pass; the table is written only if every check passes and every control holds. grpmax is the highest AC/AN among the groups the answer lists for a data type, less the excluded groups the parameters name and any group whose allele number is 0 or missing (the joint set's exclusions are this script's choice), computed from that data type's per-group counts where it passes its filters and has an allele count above 0; a tie goes to the first group in the answer's order, and grpmax is 0 where every allele is in an excluded group. faf95_max is gnomAD's fafmax.faf95_max where the data pass their filters. Numbers computed or served as floats are written with Python's '.6g' format. No structural feature is computed, and no definition of 'common' is chosen. Recorded after the run by how/runtime/channelscope/record_tables/record_table.py, from committed specs named after their tables (what/evidence_graph/curation/record_<table name>.yaml, each with its SHA-256 in recorded_tables): the run wrote its output to curation/ and no graph record, and its code, command, times and environment were read from the records this method's parameters name. records.name: channelscope.cl2.numbering
records.description: CL-2: the residue numbering of the 26 RyR1 structures of S13's table, by the rules of what/context/context_channelscope_cl2_numbering_criteria.md, version 2.2 (where it differs from 2.1; 2.1 where it differs from 2; version 2's amendments where they differ from the original rules). Each modelled residue's author number n is compared with SIFTS's UniProt position m_S (path S) and with the position m_A that this project's own alignment of the deposited sequence to the species' reference gives it (path A, M01's method A unchanged). Entities are kept as RyR1 by description and by sequence (R1a, R7, R1b); residues are classed (R3 to R10); runs of one status and offset are formed, with their identity at the species position (R11, R11c); chains and entries are labelled (R12); each departing run's boundary is read (R13); the gate residue S13 measured is read at its author number (R14); O2's reads are compared (R15). Where the criteria are silent or ambiguous, the code takes the readings GAP-01 to GAP-29, which the tables' headers print. The run refuses unless every file the script names in its run guard (DEPENDS) is in the commit and unchanged since, every input matches its retrieval record (K1) and the synthetic tests pass; the tables say that no outcome may be used if a planted fault is missed or K8 or K9 fails. The header lines record each check. records.name: channelscope.s13.gate_b_fixed
records.description: S13: the pore at the gate of the 26 RyR1 structures of O2's run and the 9ZO8/9ZOE run, measured again under criteria committed before the run (what/context/context_channelscope_s13_remeasurement_criteria.md, commit b8b2e54), by implementation A unchanged and by implementation B fixed to the gate's own height. A is O2's (`o2/gate.py`, imported by path and refused unless it hashes to the SHA-256 the script pins and O2's table's header names): its axis is the line through the centroid of the four gate residues' CA atoms, normal to their best-fit plane, and its radius the least distance from that axis to a heavy atom of the four gate residues, less the atom's radius. The fixed B keeps O2's B's parser (gemmi), chain choice (the four longest polymer chains) and axis, and reads a probe at zg*, the mean height of each chain's gate-residue heavy atom nearest the axis, over the heavy atoms within a slab 2.5 Å deep centred there. O2's B with its 3 Å window is recomputed as a second value. A radius is classed closed below 2.0 Å, open above 3.0 Å and indeterminate between. The run refuses unless every file its run guard names (DEPENDS) is in the commit it is given and unchanged since, and each coordinate file matches its retrieval record. Check S, the synthetic tests of `s13/check_gate_b_fixed.py`, runs first, and the run refuses if any fails; check R0 requires A and O2's window to equal the committed radii; check G1' compares A and the fixed B (the same class, radii within 1.0 Å); check G2' classes the two positive controls, 5TB0 closed and 5T9V open; fifteen planted faults follow, each labelled with its kind before the run. The header records each outcome.
